solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Attractive romantic heroine about to be possessed

indicators.note: the heroine's name holds the short word for about, which is taken into her possession

parts.note: Cathy is the heroine of the romantic novel Wuthering Heights
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A charming heroine of romance is on the point of being seized by passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be possessed' puts C inside CATHY.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy tune is appealing and easy to remember, so attractive in that sense.

clue.text: Songster that has been barred

parts.note: a singer locked up behind bars, read as a caged pet canary rather than a jailed vocalist

explanation.surface: A singer who has been banned from performing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barred' suggests banned; here it means kept behind the bars of a cage.
explanation.definitionFit: A songbird kept as a pet in a cage is literally a singer behind bars.

clue.text: Right-o, sweetheart!

parts.note: true means correct or right
the letter O looks like zero, which is love in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A cheerful 'Right-o!' said to a loved one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right-o' reads as agreement but splits into Right and o, the zero called love in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: One's true love is one's beloved partner or darling.

clue.text: Hearts up front — ordinary, needing to exploit crafty winger

indicators.note: places the hearts abbreviation at the very start of the answer

parts.note: H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts
to use is to exploit
fly is informal for sharp, crafty

explanation.surface: A football report: the team's attack needs an ordinary player to take advantage of a tricky wide man.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts sounds like the Scottish football club, and 'winger' like a wide player; it is an insect with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A common fly is a creature with wings, so a winger in a playful sense.

clue.text: Platform for small restaurant, some say, to get touted around

indicators.note: the word for having been touted wraps round the eatery

parts.note: touted goods are offered for sale and so sold
caff is colloquial British for a small cheap cafe

explanation.surface: A stage meant for a little eatery is hawked about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the container. A caff is a British greasy-spoon cafe, and 'some say' marks it as colloquial.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffold is a raised platform, especially one used for builders or executions.

clue.text: Agree periodic payment is coming together

parts.note: to concur is to agree
rent is paid at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Agreeing that a regular payment is due.
explanation.definitionFit: Concurrent events happen at the same time, converging or running together.

clue.text: It comes between one landing and the next

definitions.text: It comes between one landing and the next

parts.words: It comes between one landing and the next
parts.note: reads like an aircraft's journey between touchdowns, but also a set of stairs between floors

explanation.surface: Something that happens between one landing and the next.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses work: a trip by plane between landings, and a run of stairs between two landings of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is both a journey by air and a set of stairs between floors.

clue.text: Yogurts carry evenly separated elements, causing complaint

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters, second, fourth and so on, are taken from the words

explanation.surface: Yogurt pots carrying separated ingredients cause customers to grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a strong public protest or complaint.

clue.text: Bird following river in twittering host on air

indicators.note: the bird comes after the river in the answer

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a jay is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A bird after a river, chirping away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twittering' seems to describe the bird, but belongs to the definition: a disc jockey chatters on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc jockey is a radio presenter who chats between records, hence a host on air.

clue.text: Dig out food on table?

definitions.meaning: to uproot something from the soil
the call announcing that a meal is served

explanation.definitionFit: To grub up is to dig out; the cry 'grub up' tells people food is ready.

clue.text: Eagerly waiting for rum to pine to

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd or strange, so the letters are oddly rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to long for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' reads as the drink but means odd, signalling the rearrangement of TO PINE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing high on the toes in excitement is a picture of eager anticipation.

clue.text: Unwell between the sheets yet supposed to be taking part

indicators.note: the sickness word goes into the middle of the bedding word

parts.note: between the sheets means in bed
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Sick in bed, yet expected to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' signals the container; 'the sheets' stands for being in bed, and billed is used of performers due to appear.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer billed to appear is advertised as due to take part.

clue.text: Joy's plant, left by bishop

definitions.note: read as joy is, so the definition is just joy

indicators.note: the bishop has departed from the plant name

parts.note: euphorbia is the spurge family of plants
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: Joy has a plant bequeathed by a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left by' looks like a bequest; it means the bishop's B has gone from EUPHORBIA, a spurge.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoria is a feeling of intense happiness or elation.

clue.text: A time and place — rest will go round old city when one likes

indicators.note: the restful word surrounds the ancient city

parts.note: ease means rest or relaxation
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A suggested meeting time and place, with a rest stop visiting an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will go round' gives EASURE; 'rest' looks like a noun for leftovers but means relaxation.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at pleasure means doing it whenever one wishes.

clue.text: Party politician may pen article spilling secrets

indicators.note: the party and politician together enclose the article, as in a pen

parts.note: a revel is a lively party
a Tory is a British Conservative
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A party politician may write a piece leaking confidential information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may pen' sets the article between party and politician; 'pen' suggests writing, but means enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: Something revelatory discloses what was hidden, giving away secrets.

clue.text: Fusspot left label outside

indicators.note: the label wraps around the letter for left

parts.note: a sticker is an adhesive label

explanation.surface: A fussy person left a tag on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts L inside STICKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exactness, the very type of a fussy perfectionist.

clue.text: Number of copies made from photograph on course

indicators.note: in a down answer the photo word sits on top of the course word

parts.note: a print is a photograph
a run is a course, as in a ski run

explanation.surface: Copies made of a photo taken on a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A print run is the quantity of a book or paper produced in one go.

clue.text: Drug needed on Arctic manoeuvres

indicators.note: the letters are moved about like troops on exercise

explanation.surface: Medication required on polar military exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' rearranges ON ARCTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is an opiate or other substance that dulls the senses.

clue.text: High-flier's song which holds the opening to top places to see stars

indicators.note: the aircraft and song together enclose a letter between them

parts.note: a plane is something that flies high
an aria is an operatic song

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: An ambitious star's top song opens the way to celebrity venues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which holds' sets the T from 'the opening to top' between aircraft and song; 'High-flier' suggests a go-getter.
explanation.definitionFit: Planetaria are domed theatres projecting images of the night sky.

clue.text: Scoop: Rex to appear in something absorbing

indicators.note: the king's letter goes inside the absorbent item

parts.note: a towel absorbs water
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A news exclusive: the king will feature in something gripping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoop' reads as a news exclusive; 'absorbing' as gripping, but it means soaking up.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden trowel is a small hand tool used for scooping soil.

clue.text: Stationary in street, meeting a jerk

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Standing still in the road, encountering an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' suggests a fool, but here it is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means unmoving, fixed in one place.

clue.text: Waif's staggering, topless … and bottomless

definitions.note: read as waif is, so the definition is just waif

indicators.note: the final letter is removed too
the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: lurching means staggering

explanation.surface: A ragged child stumbles about, missing a top and trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes L off the front of LURCHING and 'and bottomless' takes G off the end. The ellipsis keeps the surface's comic picture going.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is a poor, ragged child, a stray like a waif.

clue.text: Clubman sounds revolutionary!

parts.note: a member of a service club whose title suggests something that rotates, not a political rebel

explanation.surface: A club member appears to be a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolutionary suggests rebellion; here it hints at rotating, after the Rotary club's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of Rotary International, the service club, is known by this title.

clue.text: Pretty self-contained — nice conversion

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for self-contained in property adverts

indicators.note: the letters undergo a conversion into a new order

explanation.surface: A flat ad: fairly self-contained, a pleasant conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' rearranges NICE into ENIC. SC is estate-agent shorthand for self-contained flats.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenic means picturesque, attractive to look at.

clue.text: Clock off and take care!

parts.note: a watch is a timepiece, a clock worn on the wrist
out means off, as a light switched off

explanation.surface: Finish work and be careful!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock off' reads as finish work.
explanation.definitionFit: The warning cry tells someone to be careful.

clue.text: Treacle endlessly refined to make booze

indicators.note: the remaining letters are refined into a new arrangement
the last letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: Treacle continually purified into alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final E of Treacle; 'refined' rearranges TREACL.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is red Bordeaux wine, a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Allowed to break silence before start of day

indicators.note: the word is broken up and reassembled
the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Permitted to break the quiet before dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' gives the British noun spelling LICENSE, used here only as letters; 'start of day' adds D.
explanation.definitionFit: Being licensed means having official permission to do something.

clue.text: Sneering single man's in charge

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A mocking bachelor is the one in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single man' suggests a bachelor, but I and RON are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironic remarks are mocking, saying the opposite of what is meant.
